browser_artifact.note: Built with cargo build --release --locked --target wasm32-unknown-unknown -p anny-wasm, then wasm-bindgen --target web. The size alone does not identify this artifact: a rebuild at a later source revision produced the same 2,321,153 bytes with a different digest, because panic locations embed file and line. Both browser suites were re-run against the digest recorded here.

browser_editor_execution: Chromium 145.0.7632.6 through examples/qualification/editor-smoke.cjs (developer-only, not run by CI): 14/14 checks passed with no page errors and a clean console - panels built from describe(), a panel slider that moves the mesh, the same parameter through the editor's own entry point, posing through the pose session, an exact return to rest, GLB export accepted by the official glTF validator (0 errors, skins present), state save/load round trip, seeded randomisation, a texture applied to the material, clip playback, and 27,420 triangles drawn
browser_execution: Chromium 145.0.7632.6 through examples/qualification/browser.cjs (developer-only, not run by CI): full smoke passed with no page errors, including the f64 and f32 pose sessions matching evaluate exactly and surviving their model being freed
browser_webgpu_execution: Google Chrome 152.0.7977.64 through examples/qualification/webgpu-smoke.cjs (system Chrome via CHROMIUM_PATH, --enable-unsafe-webgpu; developer-only, not run by CI): 7/7 checks passed against the same anny_wasm_bg.wasm (2,321,153 bytes) the editor suite passes 14/14 with. navigator.gpu present, the four GPU exports bound, the default character's own coefficients (128 of 2496 nonzero, 5.13%), WebGPU output worst absolute difference 0 vs the f32 CPU reference over 4 x 41,154 values at batch 4 and 0 again on a second run, no page errors. Adapter name redacted by Chrome; reported as ' [BrowserWebGpu]', so the backend - not the name - is what proves the call went through WebGPU
c_abi_smoke: ABI 1: 13718 vertices, 27420 faces; pose sessions match evaluate exactly (f64+f32) and survive anny_model_free
gpu_parity: crates/anny-gpu/tests/parity.rs under ANNY_REQUIRE_GPU=1 on an NVIDIA RTX 3090 (Vulkan): the GPU kernel matches anny_core::typed::apply_blendshapes within 1e-5 absolute for synthetic vectors (9.5e-7 at batch 1, 1.4e-6 at 4, 1.6e-6 at 16, 1.9e-6 at 64) and for coefficients taken from the shipped phenotype path (1.8e-7 for the default character, 2.4e-7 for a batch nudged by 0.02, 4.8e-7 for a batch spread across the phenotype range); the resident-weights path reproduces the one-shot path bit for bit and the llvmpipe control is bit-exact
native_tests_detail: cargo test --workspace --release: 101 passed, 0 failed, 16 ignored across 34 suites (2026-09-15; 3 of the passing tests are the GPU parity cases under ANNY_REQUIRE_GPU=1)
payload_reproducible: the same build writes byte-identical prepared payloads (f64 and f32) in every process; the safetensors header is re-emitted with its keys sorted because the crate serializes __metadata__ straight out of a HashMap

unity_animation.note: AnimationClip baked from native evaluations via AnnyClipBaker; sampling the clip with AnimationClip.SampleAnimation reproduces every bone's world position

unity_humanoid.note: Unity's own verdict on the avatar AnnyHumanoid.Build returns for the anny rig's unmodified hierarchy; the 50 bones the humanoid definition cannot carry are named in integrations/unity/README.md, so humanoid playback approximates Anny's pose while baked Anny clips stay exact

unity_physics.note: Skinned mode: the collider is the character's bind-pose surface; Exact mode: the collider follows the evaluated surface and is re-cooked on evaluation

unity_players.note: Both players build from the same scene and generate the same character through the native plugin. Geometry, topology, influence width and signed volume are identical across backends; the signed volume differs only in the last float digit. Each run also measures the per-update cost in the player and checks that AnnyCharacter.Evaluations advanced by exactly two per measured iteration.
